subject: Performance & context sizing follow-up: latency, concurrency, streaming checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Aisha Bhattacharya <aisha@novadocs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance & context sizing follow-up: latency, concurrency, streaming checklist

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and the technical items we'll need to qualify the SLOs you described (you mentioned 95th pctl latency targets and streaming for interactive review). I've summarized assumptions and a short checklist below so we can size Dedicated capacity or recommend a hosted configuration.

Summary of customer goals (as we heard them):
- Interactive document assistant with streaming responses for highlighted passages (near real-time UI updates).
- Target P95 latency (time-to-first-token) of <= 300ms for short queries (~100 input tokens), and tail under 500ms for more complex prompts.
- Baseline concurrency: ~120 active users concurrently, with spike tolerance to 400 concurrent sessions during peak (end-of-quarter).
- Throughput: estimate ~35k generated tokens per minute at peak; average prompt size ~300 input tokens, expected output 150 tokens.

Key context / tokenization items to confirm:
1) Input + output context window expectations (max tokens): you mentioned some long-context use cases up to 6k tokens. Please confirm maximum prompt size we must support and if you need full-document grounding (entire doc in prompt) vs embeddings-based retrieval.
2) Streaming fidelity: do you need word-by-word token streaming (low-latency token flush) or chunked sentence commits (250ms batching ok)?
3) Concurrency distribution: are the 400 concurrent sessions uniformly small (lots of 1–2 token interactions) or heavy (multi-turn with long contexts and multi-100-token outputs)?
4) Acceptable bandwidth vs cost tradeoffs: are you open to a mixed routing policy (small responses -> hosted LLM fast path; large contexts -> dedicated/quantized variant)?

Preliminary performance implications (what we discussed):
- Larger input windows (4k–8k tokens) increase memory pressure and reduce effective batch sizes, which raises p95 latency for heavy prompts unless we route to dedicated GPU capacity with higher memory models.
- Streaming low-latency first-token requires smaller batches and aggressive KV-cache reuse; that favors reserved capacity to keep hot KV cache entries and avoid cold starts.
- Concurrency spikes favor autoscaling pools; we should define warm-up and pre-provision rules for the peak windows to avoid degraded latency during sudden bursts.

Immediate next steps (action items):
- Aisha: confirm the "max prompt" number (input tokens) and share a sample doc + top-50 user flows (due 2027-04-20).
- Marissa: run a quick estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted cost at 120 steady concurrency and 400 peak (deliver by 2027-04-19).
- Diego: propose a candidate model family (2 variants: streaming-optimized low latency, and high-context quantized variant) and note expected p95 ranges (deliver by 2027-04-19).

I'll follow up with a short checklist you can fill; once we have sample payloads we'll run a small perf sim and provide a recommended config.

Thanks —
Jordan
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com | +1 415-555-0147

Attachments: token_profile.csv (sample tokenized prompts), network_latency-trace.png (demo trace)

From: Aisha Bhattacharya <aisha@novadocs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: sales_ops@novadocs.com
Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance & context sizing follow-up: latency, concurrency, streaming checklist

Thanks Jordan — great summary. A few clarifications inline and answers to your checklist: 

1) Max prompt: we need to support up to 6,144 tokens occasionally (long document lookup), but most interactions (~85%) are 400 tokens or less. We plan to use retrieval-augmented prompts for full-doc cases; we may pass entire sections for some workflows.
2) Streaming fidelity: prefer token-level streaming that displays partial completions as they are generated. UX team expects ~150ms time-to-first-token ideal, but we can tolerate up to 300ms.
3) Concurrency: distribution is skewed — 70% lightweight (short queries), 30% heavy (multi-turn with long contexts). Spikes happen predictably during business hours and at month-end reports.
4) Cost tradeoffs: open to hybrid routing. We'd like recommendations on when to prefer a quantized variant vs a full-precision instance.

I've attached a small sample set (shared via Drive link) and the tokenized breakdown for three representative flows. We'll fill the checklist by tomorrow.

Best,
Aisha
Head of Product | NovaDocs
aisha@novadocs.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance & context sizing follow-up: latency, concurrency, streaming checklist

Jordan / Marissa —

Quick tech notes after reviewing the sample payloads Aisha shared (thanks):
- For the "heavy" flow (avg input 3.2k tokens, output 300 tokens): estimate tokens-in-flight ~3.5k. Model memory: prefer a 40B-class with 48GB GPU RAM or a quantized 70B on 80GB memory depending on quality tolerance.
- Streaming-optimized path: use a lower-latency model family with attention optimizations and a small per-request prefill (we can cap prefix batching to 2–4 requests to hit ~150–250ms first-token P95 for short prompts).
- Batching strategy: for bursty short requests, target 4–8ms token-generation latency per token with continuous batching; for large contexts, fall back to per-request execution to avoid batch-induced memory blowups.
- KV cache: recommend sticky routing to warm instances for active users (session affinity) to reuse KV cache across turns — important to keep P95 stable.

Cost/Capacity recommendation (very rough):
- Steady baseline: hosted with autoscaling + one Dedicated pool sized for heavy prompts during business hours (2 x 80GB GPUs) — this reduces cold-starts and keeps streaming latency predictable.
- Peak protection: pre-warm N extra instances 30 minutes before known spikes (month-end) using synthetic warm-up traffic.

I'll produce a short runbook with expected P95 for each model variant and a recommended routing policy (hybrid) by EOD 2027-04-19.

Diego
Principal Applied ML Eng | Redwood Inference
